text: The study was a dim, old fashioned chamber, festooned with cobwebs and sprinkled with antique dust, where tall bookcases of oak lined the walls. <break time="0.8s" /> Over the central bookcase stood a bronze bust of Hippocrates, with which, according to some authorities, Doctor Heidegger was accustomed to consult in all difficult cases. <break time="0.8s" /> In the darkest corner hung a tall, narrow mirror, within which, it was fabled, the spirits of all the doctors dead patients dwelt. <break time="0.8s" /> The opposite side of the room was ornamented with the portrait of a young lady who, many years before, had been on the point of marrying Doctor Heidegger. <break time="0.8s" /> But, being affected with some slight disorder, she had swallowed one of her lovers prescriptions and died on the bridal evening. <break time="0.8s" /> The greatest curiosity of the study was a ponderous book, bound in black leather, which was well known to be a book of magic. <break time="0.8s" /> On the summer afternoon of our tale, a round table stood in the middle of the room, and on it was placed a cut glass vase of beautiful form. <break time="0.8s" /> The sunshine came through the window and fell upon the vase, so that a mild splendor was reflected from it onto the ashen faces of the five old people.
